question: Po letnej búrke sa vám na diaľnici vyjasní a chcete zahliadnuť dúhu. Ak viete, kde je práve slnko, kam sa musíte pozrieť?
source_excerpt: the centre of the rainbow is the antisolar point

extra.why_interesting: People see rainbows after storms but rarely notice the rule behind them. A player can work it out on the spot from memories of seeing one, and the explanation adds why rainbows don't appear at summer noon.
extra.verification_notes: Rainbows appear in the direction opposite the sun (the antisolar point), as described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow; I did not run a search or check the quote on the page.

explanation: Dúha je vždy na opačnej strane oblohy ako slnko, takže ho musíte mať za chrbtom. Preto ju na poludnie v lete takmer neuvidíte, lebo slnko je vtedy príliš vysoko a dúha by sa schovala pod obzor.

question: Cestou autom zbadáte blesk a začnete pomaly počítať. Hrom zaduní až po šiestich sekundách. Približne ako ďaleko od vás udrel blesk?
source_excerpt: Divide the seconds between flash and thunder by three to get kilometers; sound travels about 340 m/s.

extra.why_interesting: Players have seen lightning and heard thunder all their lives but rarely turn the gap into a distance. With a hint of physics, or the half-remembered rule of 3 seconds per km, they can work it out in the car, which gives the 'I can work this out!' feeling.
extra.verification_notes: Speed of sound ~343 m/s gives 6 s ≈ 2 km, consistent with the 3 seconds per km rule of thumb.

explanation: Svetlo z blesku k vám dorazí takmer okamžite, ale zvuk prejde vzduchom len asi 340 metrov za sekundu, teda zhruba kilometer za tri sekundy. Stačí teda počet sekúnd vydeliť tromi a viete, ako ďaleko je búrka.
